faqs.a: Yes, digital dental X-rays use a low dose of radiation, lower than traditional film X-rays, and dentists take them only when they are needed for diagnosis. If you are pregnant or might be, tell your dentist so they can decide whether the X-ray is necessary and take extra precautions.

faqs.q: Is laser dentistry better than traditional dental treatment?
faqs.a: Laser dentistry can make some procedures, especially gum treatments, less invasive, with less bleeding, fewer stitches and quicker healing. It is not suitable for every treatment, so your dentist will choose between a laser and conventional methods based on your specific problem.

faqs.q: Can a dentist diagnose a dental problem through an online consultation?
faqs.a: Only partly. A video consultation can help a dentist understand your symptoms, give initial advice and judge how urgent the problem is. Most dental problems still need an in-person examination, and often X-rays, before a diagnosis can be confirmed and treatment given.

faqs.q: Can artificial intelligence replace a dentist?
faqs.a: No. AI tools can help dentists by analysing X-rays and scans to flag possible problems such as early cavities, but diagnosis and treatment decisions are still made by a qualified dentist. AI is best seen as support for the dentist's judgement rather than a replacement for it.
